atoms.text: Arthur wants to do an experiment to find out more about the effect of temperature on the dissolution rate of sugar.

instruction.text: What must he keep the same to ensure a fair test?

atoms.b: Arthur mixes the same amount of sugar into 3 glasses of water with equal volumes. The temperature of the water ((++increases decreases)) by ((++6 7 8)) degrees between each glass from left to right.

instruction.text: Draw a line to connect the points on the graph to identify the trend in Arthur’s experiment.

atoms.a: Arthur predicted that the sugar would dissolve faster in water with a lower temperature. Was he correct?
Using the line, how long would it take for the sugar to dissolve at 6°C?

atoms.b: Arthur now wants to see if the ((++type price packaging)) of sugar affects its dissolution rate.

Arthur labels the sugar he has from left to right:
1: ((++white_sugar white_sugar_cubes brown_sugar))
2: ((white_sugar white_sugar_cubes ++brown_sugar))
3: ((white_sugar ++white_sugar_cubes brown_sugar))

instruction.text: Use Arthur’s notes to sort the dissolution rates of sugar from fastest to slowest.
Arthur predicted that the white sugar cubes would take the longest to dissolve due to their shape.

feedback.end: Although the white sugar cubes did take longer to dissolve than the white sugar, the brown sugar took even longer. Brown sugar is less refined and often contains molasses - a material that makes brown sugar dense and slow to dissolve.
